notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-09-04. Both findings, at their source.

FINDING 1 — two compounding defects, neither in the EOS (the bead's own evidence that ln_phi is healthy at 400-600 K was right; the solver goes far higher than that):

  (a) CubicEos::select_root accepted a compressibility root at or below the covolume B. ln_phi then evaluates ln(Z - B) on a negative argument and returns Some(vec![NaN, ..]) rather than None, so k_values' existing 'no usable root -> Wilson' fallback never fired and NaN propagated. Measured: PR liquid ln_phi is NaN from ~1500 K up, well above the slate's highest Tc of 981 K. select_root now requires Z > B for both phases, restoring the meaning of the Option.

  (b) Above the critical region both phases return the SAME root, so every K collapses to 1 and the bubble residual decays asymptotically to 0 without crossing. solve_scalar's expansion moves whichever endpoint has the smaller |residual| — precisely the wrong move against an asymptote — so it chased it away from the real root and reported NoBracket with best |residual| = 1.1e-16. Added scan_for_bracket: on NoBracket or a trivial converged result, sweep the interval and take the LOWEST non-degenerate sign change, which is the physical bubble point. The scan skips degenerate stretches, which exist at BOTH ends of the range, not just the top.

Measured on the reference crude column (12 stages, 8 pseudo-components, 1.2 bar), all monotonic:
  Ideal             T 423.6 -> 588.5 K
  PengRobinson      T 424.9 -> 586.1 K
  PengRobinson1978  T 424.9 -> 586.9 K
  Srk               T 424.8 -> 586.4 K
The three cubics agreeing with each other and with Ideal is the cross-check that they are on the physical root.

FINDING 2 — columns::bubble_point::check_monotonic_temperature now rejects a converged profile whose temperature falls going down the column, with a message that says so. Stages carrying a specified heat duty are exempt: an intercooler legitimately reverses the gradient. 4 unit tests including the exact dip shape the bead describes.

Also added SaturationError::TrivialSolution so a K = 1 'solution' can never be returned as a saturation point. A single component is exempt — for pure i the residual IS K - 1, so K = 1 is what Tsat means, and testing for triviality there would reject every correct answer (caught by 4 pre-existing single-component flash tests).

CrudeColumnConfig gains a `package` field defaulting to PengRobinson1978; the Ideal pin and its explanatory comment are gone. 678 tests pass.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
CORRECTION to my earlier notes on this bead, after pulling 44a2001339 (fixed by another machine).

My diagnosis was RIGHT IN ITS EVIDENCE AND WRONG IN ITS CONCLUSION. I reported that CubicEos::ln_phi returns finite liquid and vapour fugacity coefficients across 400-600 K for both PR and PR78, and concluded the EOS was healthy and the defect lay elsewhere in the bubble-point iteration.

The evidence was true. The conclusion was wrong because I checked the wrong range: THE BUBBLE-POINT SOLVER EXPLORES TO ROUGHLY 1950 K, not 600 K. The actual defect was in the cubic path after all — select_root accepted a compressibility root at or below the covolume B, so ln_phi evaluated ln(Z - B) on a negative argument and returned Some(vec![NaN, ...]) rather than None, which defeated k_values existing no-usable-root fallback.

The lesson worth keeping: I probed the range the COLUMN operates in, not the range the SOLVER searches. Those are different, and only the second one bounds where a numerical failure can occur.

Consequence for what I wrote elsewhere: my claim that PR78 was "necessary but not sufficient" is superseded. With the cubic path fixed, PR78 is now the DEFAULT package for the crude column and it solves — 34 iterations, error 8.875e-7, monotonic profile. The doc comments in crude_distillation.rs have been re-measured and corrected.

One finding survives and is worth keeping: on ideal K-values, no cut point gave a CONVERGED but non-monotonic profile; on PR78 the same case reports NotConverged after 100 iterations at error 5.9e-3. The cubic path fails honestly where the ideal path failed silently. The underlying complaint — that a solver can report success on a physically impossible profile — is unchanged and still deserves a monotonicity check.

title: columns: bubble-point solver fails with ANY cubic package; and reports success on non-physical profiles

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
3 of 4 BCs fully ported (agent pass, 2026-07-15) under src/genfoam/thermal_hydraulics/boundary_conditions/:
- blackbody_radiation.rs (317 LOC): BlackBodyRadiationBc — Stefan-Boltzmann wall temp from a Fourier heat-flux estimate. 4 tests incl. 3 V&V (closed-form Stefan-Boltzmann inversion, hand-computed Fourier flux, composed full-step), all passing.
- velocity_rundown.rs (208 LOC): VelocityRundownBc — power-law pump/flow coastdown U(t)=U0*(A+B*(t-t0))^C. 3 tests incl. 1 V&V (hand-computed power-law factor), all passing.
- time_field_table.rs (299 LOC): TimeFieldTable — per-face time-tabulated scalar BC; reuses ScalarInterpolateTable (one instance per face column) rather than new math. 6 unit tests, all passing.
- nusselt_baffle.rs (180 LOC): NusseltThermalBaffle1DBc — SCAFFOLD ONLY, data-shape + unimplemented!() methods. Not ported: the master/slave implicit cross-patch coupling doesn't fit the "pure closure" contract used here; needs op-p6p.7.11 (porous solver) to land first to decide how inter-patch coupling is represented. Follow-up bead needed for the real port.

Verification: whole-crate build is currently broken by concurrent sibling edits (multi_region/mesh_region.rs, thermal_hydraulics/solver/one_phase.rs — not touched by this bead). Built + ran all 22 tests green (incl. clippy clean, Android aarch64-linux-android check clean) in an isolated scratch crate mirroring the real module tree/deps, since cargo test -p outram-foam-appbuilder-lib couldn't run end-to-end. Re-run cargo test -p outram-foam-appbuilder-lib --lib --release boundary_conditions once sibling breakage clears, to confirm in-tree.

Not yet done: full NusseltThermalBaffle1D port (this bead's remaining scope, or split to a follow-up bead).

description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #32 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/32), maintainer: 'kovan-cli should import the token savings features of kopitiam-cli, by wiring the api in directly. then we shld be able to have kovan-cli generate skill.md also for AI agents to read. Then after this, use kovan-cli for token saving features and dogfood.'

SURVEYED 2026-08-22 (read-only, ~/Documents/fun_projects/kopitiam per the workspace's consume-binaries-only rule -- this epic is about depending on specific published LIBRARY crates from that workspace, not the kopitiam/kopi-beans BINARIES the hard rule is about):

1. TOKEN COST ESTIMATE. kopitiam's 'kopitiam tokens <path>' is backed by kopitiam-tokenizer (published, AGPL-3.0-only, deps: kopitiam-core + regex + serde_json -- all lightweight, no C/BLAS/GPU) -- specifically estimate::estimate_tokens(text: &str) -> usize and estimate_tokens_by_line, a dependency-free per-Unicode-script character-weighted estimator (~25-30% accuracy vs real BPE, deliberately -- see its own module doc). kovan's own token-estimation today is kovan-semantics::agent_docs::estimated_tokens(bytes) = bytes/4 -- a much cruder heuristic, used only by 'kovan-cli agent-docs-gen --budget'. Issue #32's 'wiring the api in directly' matches the precedent already set by kopitiam-pdf (crate-local dependency in crates/kovan/Cargo.toml, never the workspace table, since kovan is already this workspace's one AGPL-3.0-only crate) -- NOT a port, a direct dependency, same boundary-exception shape.

2. OUTLINE / SLICE. kopitiam's 'outline'/'slice' are richer (rust-analyzer-backed, via kopitiam-semantic) but kovan-semantics ALREADY has ripgrep-first single-file primitives that cover the same job at the ripgrep tier: LanguageAdapter::rough_definition_pattern() + kovan_discovery::search_file(path, pattern) -> Vec<SearchMatch{line, column, text}>. No new dependency needed for a first cut -- this is a 'kovan already has 90% of this' case per the workspace's search-before-building rule.

3. SKILL.MD. kopitiam has scripts/gen-kopitiam-skill.sh -> kopitiam_skill.md (Claude Code Skill frontmatter + 'CRITICAL agent guidance' + recipes + command reference, ~1132 lines, shell-script-generated). Per this workspace's own 'no Python/scripts for documentation generation -- build it into kovan' hard rule (spirit extends to shell here too, and kovan already self-generates docs via 'kovan agent-docs-gen'/'kovan api-docs'), kovan-cli's equivalent should be a native subcommand, not a companion script.

4. CHECK/TEST --compact (diagnostics dedup, kopitiam's diagnostics.rs, ~1053 lines) and richer LSP-backed outline/refs/callers/callees (kopitiam-semantic, rust-analyzer-backed) are bigger pieces, deliberately deferred to follow-on child beads -- not blocking the first cut.
title: kovan-cli token savings — import kopitiam-cli's token-frugal features, generate skill.md, dogfood

design:
## Why

`use <crate>::prelude::*;` is the import pattern users reach for first, and it
is the only one a small model can guess without reading the source. Today it
does not reliably work in this workspace.

## Measured state (2026-09-05)

**8 of 36 crates have a prelude at all**, ranging from 2 to 44 `pub use` lines:

| has prelude | exports |
|---|---|
| outram-mc-libs | 44 |
| outram-foam-basic-lib | 35 |
| outram-foam-appbuilder-lib | 21 |
| boon-lay | 16 |
| outram-foam-turbulence-lib | 9 |
| njoy-outram-park-fork | 6 |
| tampines-steam-tables | 4 |
| outram-park-fork-offbeat | 2 |

The other 28 have none — including `teh-o-prke`, `tampines`, `raffles`,
`bedok`, `nee_soon`, `tuas_boussinesq_solver`, and every `kovan-*` crate.

## The sharper finding: a prelude nobody uses

Before this issue's first fix, **not one example in `outram-mc-libs` or
`njoy-outram-park-fork` imported from the prelude** — despite
`outram-mc-libs` having a 44-line one. Examples wrote four-segment paths like
`outram_mc_libs::material::nuclide::Nuclide` instead.

Cause, on inspection: the prelude exported 7 of the 8 symbols the examples
need. The one missing was `NuclideComponent` — which you cannot construct a
`Material` without, i.e. squarely on the critical path. One gap there sends
the reader back to deep paths for *everything else too*.

**A 95%-complete prelude gets used 0% of the time.** Completeness on the
critical path is not a nice-to-have; it is the whole value of the construct.
This is the same failure as the `Tape::read_file` case in commit 4e802927:
the better path existed, and the examples taught past it.

## Done so far

- `outram-mc-libs`: added `NuclideComponent`, re-exported `NjoyError` (the
  error type every ENDF entry point returns, previously unnameable without
  depending on `njoy-outram-park-fork` yourself).
- `njoy-outram-park-fork`: added `reconr`, `ReconrConfig`, `ReconrResult`,
  `doppler_broaden` — it exported `Tape` but none of the functions you call on one.
- Both new tutorial examples now import **nothing but** `use <crate>::prelude::*`,
  which stands as the executable proof that the prelude suffices.

## Work remaining

1. **Every crate gets a prelude.** 28 to add.
2. **Completeness test, per crate: can the crate's own examples compile with
   the prelude as their only import?** This is checkable, not a matter of
   taste, and it is the test that caught the `NuclideComponent` gap. Consider
   enforcing it in CI.
3. **Convert existing examples to prelude imports.** They are the discovery
   mechanism — an example reaching past the prelude teaches that the prelude
   is insufficient, whether or not it actually is.
4. **Document the convention** in the root `CLAUDE.md` "Human interface layer"
   section: a public item reachable only by deep path is not considered
   exposed.

## Related

- bn `op-g7cq` / gh #58 — the maturity gate. Note this work is API-usability
  work, so under that gate it is only *enforced* on crates declared mature;
  adding preludes is cheap and safe to do earlier.
- Commit 4e802927 — the first two crates.
title: Make prelude imports sufficient and Haiku-friendly in every crate
